answer: Behavioral cohort tracing detects sybils after settlement by grouping identities whose transaction timing and counterparty sets co-move beyond chance. A fable of independent agents would produce uncorrelated edges; real operators leak a spiral of synchronized actions across their puppets. The mechanism models each identity's action series against the wider ocean of activity, flagging clusters whose correlation exceeds a threshold. Each flagged identity forfeits its accumulated reputation balance, so an attacker controlling N identities pays N times the reputational loss to sustain cover.
